$comment: Behavioral tests. Each prompt should cause the named skill or command to fire and the expectations to hold. Run them by hand in a fresh Claude session after any substantive edit to a SKILL.md — a skill that stops triggering is invisible until someone notices the answers got worse.

evals.prompt: Can you analyze my SEO performance for the last month?
expect: calls get_capabilities or list_properties before analyzing
does not invent a site_url
separates branded from non-branded traffic in the report

evals.prompt: Which keywords are we closest to ranking on page one for?
expect: identifies the position 4-15 band as striking distance
names specific queries and the pages that rank for them
does not recommend generic 'improve your content'

evals.prompt: Our search traffic dropped about 30% this month. What happened?
expect: uses compare_search_periods
classifies the drop by shape before proposing a cause
does not attribute it to a Google update without ruling out the other three shapes

evals.prompt: Search Console says 'Couldn't fetch' for my sitemap. How do I fix it?
expect: explains that Google never parsed the file, so it is not a validity problem
checks status code, content type, redirects, and robots.txt
notes that a new sitemap can show this for hours or days and that resubmitting does not speed it up
does not propose deleting and resubmitting as a first move

evals.prompt: Ten of my pages say 'Crawled - currently not indexed'. How do I get them indexed?
expect: explains this is a quality judgment, not a technical fault
states that resubmission will not change it
recommends internal links and content depth

evals.prompt: Can I use IndexNow to get these pages into Google faster?
expect: states plainly that Google does not participate in IndexNow
names Bing, Yandex, Seznam, Naver as participants
does not present IndexNow as a Google indexing method

evals.prompt: The SEO reports are too generic. Can you learn about my site?
expect: derives brand terms and top pages from GSC data before asking questions
recommends storing the profile outside the plugin directory
asks which pages matter commercially, not just which get traffic

evals.prompt: The GSC tools aren't showing up in Claude at all.
expect: recognizes that skills load independently of the MCP server
directs the user to stderr lines prefixed [gsc-seo]
checks for uv/python on the launcher PATH before blaming credentials

evals.prompt: It's authenticated but list_properties comes back empty.
expect: identifies the missing Search Console user grant as the likely cause
explains the grant is per-property with no account-wide option
does not suggest recreating the service account key

evals.prompt: Just delete the old sitemap and the stale property to clean things up.
expect: explains that destructive tools are disabled by default
does not enable GSC_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE on the user's behalf
warns that deleting a property discards its history irreversibly
asks for explicit confirmation of the exact target

evals.prompt: Show me what a keyword report looks like — I haven't connected Search Console yet.
expect: uses sample-data/ rather than refusing or inventing numbers
labels the output as synthetic sample data
surfaces the planted striking-distance cluster

evals.prompt: What's the CTR on kugamon.com this month?
expect: calls list_properties rather than assuming the property exists
reports honestly if the property is not accessible
never fabricates metrics

evals.$comment: Regression: a real analysis called two sitelink pages the site's biggest anomaly and put 'investigate them' as recommendation #1. They were working correctly.
evals.prompt: This page is at average position 2.6 but its CTR is 0.18%. That's way below the benchmark — what's wrong with it?
expect: runs get_search_by_page_query before diagnosing
recognises the sitelink signature — one brand query supplying nearly all impressions at position ~1
concludes working-as-intended rather than prescribing a title rewrite
notes that sitelink impressions depress site-wide CTR averages

evals.$comment: Regression: sort_by=impressions was used and its output presented as impression-ranked. It is silently ignored by Google.
evals.prompt: Pull me the top queries by impressions for the last six months.
expect: does not rely on sort_by to produce an impression ranking
states that results come back clicks-sorted regardless of the sort argument
uses filtered pulls to reach high-impression zero-click queries
never labels a clicks-sorted list as 'top by impressions'

evals.prompt: Give me every keyword opportunity on the site.
expect: runs filtered pulls per commercially meaningful term rather than one large unsorted pull
states plainly that a filtered sweep is targeted, not exhaustive
does not claim complete coverage of the query set

evals.prompt: Why does this query get impressions but never any clicks?
expect: pulls dimensions=query,page filtered to that query
checks whether more than one page draws impressions for it
if split, recommends consolidating rather than optimising each page separately

evals.prompt: There are these huge paragraph-long queries in my Search Console data that read like AI prompts. Should I target them?
expect: identifies them as AI assistants searching on a user's behalf
advises against targeting the exact wording, which will not repeat
reads the cluster as a signal about comparison and definition content
excludes them from CTR averages
